analysis:
Documentation-only change to docs/provider/cli-reference.md. I examined the base text (lines 2392-2617) and head text (lines 1-385) of the units supplied. The patch excerpt shows the substantive change: `darkbloom sandbox setup` gains a repeatable `--disk <volume>` flag for work disks (base 1064/head 1078; new Setup bullets near head 1094-1132). The excerpt is truncated, so the remainder of the `--disk` semantics is not visible.

The lines visible to me are unchanged context, and they contain no security regressions. No code, controls or defaults change in the visible hunks. Descriptions of logout, the add-on hold, cache storage and the worker candidate match the existing threat-model language.

Relevant threat IDs: TB-013/T-061, because the sandbox setup path runs the add-on installer as the Mac's owner and A-019 is the asset at stake. The new `--disk` argument is passed on to that installer. Whether the CLI validates it correctly is not visible: the excerpt says setup makes the path absolute and checks it, but the code (SandboxEligibility/SandboxCommand) is not in this PR's supplied evidence.

Open integration questions for a later pass or the code PR:
- Does the argument passing to install.sh avoid shell injection and path traversal or symlink issues?
- Do the `/Volumes/<name>` checks resist non-local, spoofed or cloned volumes?
- Does the add-on treat an external work disk as untrusted storage? The VM images and job data would sit outside the Mac's internal disk. The T-041 cache-storage analysis (UUID cloning, retained ciphertext) may apply analogously.

The lines I could see give me no basis for a finding. I did not review the truncated remainder of the diff.
